Rashi on Shabbat 91a:1:1.english: Lest you say - Since he forgot at the time of carrying [it] out, [in] that he did not remember its storage.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:1:2.english: His intention is nullified for him - And here there is neither the significance of the intention of storing [it] away nor the intention of carrying [it] out.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:1:3.hebrew: קמ"ל - דכל העושה סתם על דעת הראשונה עושה, ובחשיבותיה קמא קאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:1:3.english: [The Gemara] teaches us - that anyone who acts without specifying [otherwise] acts with the original intent in mind, and it remains in its original significance.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:2:1.english: "Any amount," we learned - And an unattributed Mishnah is [the view of] Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:2:2.english: To exclude a dried fig-bulk - [The measure] of other foods.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:2:3.hebrew: אלא מעתה - דמתני' בדעתיה תלינן כדקאמרת, משום דעל דעת ראשונה מחשבת ליה שיעורא:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:2:3.english: But now - that [in] the Mishnah we make [the measure] depend on his intention as you say, because you calculate the measure for him according to [his] initial intention:

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:2:4.hebrew: חישב להוציא כל ביתו - בהוצאה אחת, דלא אחשבה אלא אם כן הוציא כולה כאחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:2:4.english: One who planned to carry out [the contents of] his entire house - In a single carrying out, for he did not deem it [significant] unless he carried it all out at once.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:2:5.english: So too - That when he carries it out little by little, he is not liable?

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:2:6.english: His intention is nullified - And the measure that is significant to people is [what is] significant.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:3:1.hebrew: וכל אדם אין חייבין אלא כשיעורו - ואע"פ שהוכשר לזה והצניעו:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:3:1.english: And any [other] person is only liable according to its measure - Even though it was deemed fit by this [person] and he stored it.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:4:1.hebrew: כגרוגרת - איכא שיעורא לאכילה ולהוצאה, וכ"ש לזריעה, דשיעורא בכל שהוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:4:1.english: A dried fig-bulk - There is the [requisite] measure for eating and for carrying out, and all the more so for sowing, for its measure is any amount.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:5:1.english: And it swelled - and stood at [the size of] a dried fig before placing [it down].

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:5:2.english: And he reconsidered it, to eat it - And he placed it down; what is [the law]?

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:5:3.hebrew: את"ל - בההיא, אע"ג דעקירה והנחה לאו בחדא מחשבה הואי, מיחייב:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:5:3.english: If you say - In that [case], even though the lifting and the placing were not [done] with one intention, he is liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:5:4.hebrew: התם הוא דזיל הכא כו' - בשעת מחשבה ראשונה היה בו כשיעור למחשבתו ושיעור למחשבה שניה, הלכך, מיצטרפי עקירה והנחה:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:5:4.english: There, it is [because] go here, etc. - At the time of [his] first intention, it had the [requisite] measure for his [first] intention, and [now it has] the [requisite] measure for [his] second intention; therefore, the lifting and the placing combine.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:5:5.hebrew: אבל הכא בעידנא דאפקה לא הוה בה שיעור - למחשבה שניה של הנחה, ולא מצטרפי הנחה לעקירה:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:5:5.english: But here, at the time he carried it out, it did not have the measure - for the second intention [at the time] of placing down, and the placing down does not combine with the lifting up.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:5:6.english: Since had he been silent - At this second [stage], it has the measure for sowing, and he is liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:5:7.hebrew: השתא נמי מיחייב - הואיל ויש שיעור למחשבה אחרונה, ובשיעור זה איכא שיעורא למחשבה ראשונה ויותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:5:7.english: Now too, he is liable - Since there is [the required] measure for the final intention, and in this measure there is [the required] measure for the initial intention, and more.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:6:1.english: He is not liable - For at the time of placing [it down], there is not the [required] measure for the original intention.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:6:2.english: After the present - We follow the present intention with regard to placing [it down].

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:6:3.hebrew: יש דיחוי - מה שחסרה בינתים, אילו אנחה בההיא שעתא לא מיחייב — מי אמרינן תורת דיחוי, דנדחה לו מחיוב חטאת ובטלה לה עקירה, וכי הדר תפחה והניחה, הוי הנחה בלא עקירה:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:6:3.english: Is there disqualification - In that it became deficient in the meantime — [such that] had he placed it down at that moment he would not be liable — do we say [that] the principle of disqualification [applies], so that it is disqualified for him from liability for a sin-offering and the lifting is nullified, and when it subsequently expands and he places it down, it is a placing without a lifting?

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:7:1.hebrew: אי לענין טומאה - דמיבעיא לך אם נטמא לטמא טומאת אוכלין או לאו, כביצה בעינן:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:7:1.english: If with regard to ritual impurity - [Meaning] that you are asking whether [it] becomes impure to convey food impurity or not, we require an egg-bulk.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:7:2.hebrew: והאי משלימו - שנחה אצלו והשלימו, וע"י הנחה זו נטמאו:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:7:2.english: And this completes it - For [the terumah] came to rest beside it and completed it, and through this coming to rest they became impure.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:7:4.hebrew: שיעורן כגרוגרת - אם הוציאן לרה"ר בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:7:4.english: Their measure is a dried fig-bulk - If one carried them out to the public domain on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 91a:7:5.hebrew: ואמאי לימא - בכזית מיחייב, דהא חשיבה הוצאה לענין איפסולי ביוצא, דאי אכליה הוא עובר בלאו. דכל שבקודש פסול, בא הכתוב ליתן לא תעשה על אכילתו, ואכילה בכזית:
Rashi on Shabbat 91a:7:5.english: And why? Let us say - [that] he is liable for an olive-bulk, for [the] carrying out is considered significant with respect to becoming disqualified as yotzei [having left its permitted boundary], since if he eats it, he transgresses a negative commandment. For [regarding] anything sacred that is disqualified, Scripture came to establish a negative commandment against eating it, and [the minimum measure for] eating is an olive-bulk.

Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:2:1.hebrew: מתקיף לה רב יצחק - פירש בקונטרס דפריך אאביי, וקשה: דאמאי נטר ליה עד הכא? ואומר הרב פור"ת בשם רבינו שמואל: דאדרב יהודה אבוה פריך, וה"פ: כיון דאמרת דמוציא חטה אחת לזריעה חייב אע"פ שאין רגילות, משום דבתר מחשבתו אזלינן — ה"נ כשחישב להוציא כל ביתו ניזול בתר מחשבתו, ולא נחייבנו בפחות, כיון דפחות מיכן אינו חשוב בעיניו. ומשני: התם בטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם, דאין אדם שלא יהא חשוב בעיניו פחות מכן; אבל הכא יש בני אדם שחשובה להם חטה אחת לזריעה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:2:1.english: Rav Yitzḥak strongly objects to this - Rashi explained that he is raising an objection against Abaye, and [this] is difficult: why did he wait for him until here? And Rabbi Porat says in the name of Rabbeinu Shmuel that he is raising an objection against Rav Yehuda, his father, and this is its explanation: Since you said that one who carries out a single wheat [seed] for sowing is liable even though it is not usual, because we follow his intention — so too, when one intended to carry out [the contents of] his entire house, let us follow his intention and not hold him liable for less, since less than this is not significant in his eyes. And [the Gemara] answers: There, his intention is nullified vis-à-vis all people, for there is no person for whom less than this is not significant in his eyes; but here, there are people for whom a single wheat [seed] is significant for sowing.

Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:5:1.hebrew: או דילמא בתר השתא אזלינן - משמע דאי בתר השתא אזלינן, ליכא למיבעיא מידי, מדקאמר את"ל: "בתר השתא אזלינן, הוציא גרוגרת לאכילה וצמקה וחזרה ותפחה, מהו?", ולא מיבעיא ליה אקמייתא. ואמאי? אכתי תיבעי ליה אי הוה דיחוי אצל שבת או לא, כדבעי בסמוך, דהא מיד כשצמקה נדחית! וי"ל, דדוקא ההיא דבסמוך חשיב ליה דיחוי, שנדחית בין משיעור ראשון בין משיעור אחרון; אבל הכא, דמשיעור אחרון מיהא לא נדחית — לא חשיב ליה דיחוי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:5:1.english: Or perhaps we follow [the situation at] present - This implies that if we follow the present [situation], there is nothing to ask [i.e., there is no dilemma], from the fact that [the Gemara] says: "If you say that we follow the present, [then if] one carried out a dried fig-bulk for eating, and it shriveled, and then it expanded, what [is the law]?" — and it does not ask about the earlier [case]. But why [not]? Let it still ask whether there is disqualification with regard to Shabbat or not, as it asks immediately following, for as soon as it shriveled, it became disqualified! And one can answer that specifically [in] that [case] immediately following, it is considered disqualification, because it was disqualified from both the first measure and the final measure; whereas here, since it was at least not disqualified from the final measure, it is not considered disqualification.

Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:7:1.hebrew: אי לענין טומאה כביצה אוכלין בעינן - משמע דלא מקבל אוכל טומאה בפחות מכביצה. ומה שהביא רש"י מת"כ דאוכל מקבל טומאה בכל שהוא, דתניא: "מכל האוכל" — שמטמא בכל שהוא; יכול יהא מטמא אחרים? ת"ל: "אשר יאכל" — אוכל הנאכל בבת אחת, הוי אומר זה ביצת תרנגולת — אומר ר"ת דאסמכתא היא, דה"נ מעשר ירק מרבינן בת"כ מ"וכל מעשר הארץ", ולא הוי אלא אסמכתא בעלמא. והא דפריך בפרק כל שעה (פסחים ד' לג:) למ"ד משקין מיבלע בליעי מהא דתנן: "טמא מת שסחט זיתים וענבים כביצה מכוונת — טהורים", ואי מיבלע בליעי אמאי טהורים? ומוקי לה בענבים שלא הוכשרו; לאימת קא מיתכשרי? לכי סחיט להו, וכי סחיט להו בציר ליה שיעוריה — אתי שפיר גם לפי' הקונטרס, דאע"ג דמקבל טומאה בכל שהוא, מ"מ בציר ליה שיעורא מלקבל הכשר, לפירוש הרב פור"ת דמפרש בשם רש"י בפ' חבית (לקמן שבת קמה.) דאין אוכל מקבל הכשר בפחות מכביצה, וטעמא משום דמ"אשר יאכל" נפקא לן לטמא אחרים בכביצה, ואהא כתב "אשר יבא עליו מים". וכן בפרק אלו עוברין (פסחים מה.) גבי בצק שבסידקי עריבה, דמפרש אביי כגון דאיכא פחות מכביצה אוכלין ונגעו בהאי בצק בפסח דאיסורו חושבו מצטרף, אע"ג דבלא צירוף פחות מכביצה הוה מצי לאוקמי דנגע שרץ בכזית שבסידקי עריבה בפסח דאיסורו חושבו מקבל טומאה — בשאר ימות השנה אי קפיד אין, אי לא לא — אלא דלענין קבלת טומאה עצמה לא נפקא לן מינה מידי, דבלאו הכי אסורה משום חמץ, להכי נקט לענין לטמא אחרים. ומייתי רבינו תם ראיה דאין אוכל מקבל טומאה פחות מכביצה, דתניא בפרק אלו עוברין (פסחים מד.): "המקפה של תרומה, השום והשמן של חולין, ונגע טבול יום במקצתן — פסל את כולן; מקפה של חולין, ושום ושמן של תרומה, ונגע טבול יום במקצתן — לא פסל אלא מקום מגעו", והוינן בה: מקום מגעו אמאי פסל, והא לא הוי כביצה? ורש"י ל"ג הכי, אלא גריס "והא בטל ברובא", ומפרש דהכי פריך: מקום מגעו אמאי פסול, והא בטל שום ושמן אגב מקפה, דהא משום הכי קתני ברישא "פסל את כולן"? ואין נראה למחוק הספרים. ועוד, נהי דבטלי ברישא להחמיר, להקל לא אמרינן דבטלי! ועוד, דלא שייך למימר דבטלי השום והשמן, כיון שהן בעין, מדקתני "לא פסל אלא מקום מגעו". ועוד (דתניא בתוספתא): "בד"א? בזמן שהיא גוש בקערה" — משמע שהן בעין. ואין להאריך. ורש"י חזר בו בכריתות (דף כא.), וגבי "פרה מיטמא טומאת אוכלין" (חולין דף פב.). והא דאמר בפ"ק דחולין (דף כד:): "התורה העידה על כלי חרס אפילו מלא חרדל" — לאו דוקא חרדל, אלא כלומר מלא ביצים; ומשום דבחרדל איכא טובא — ראשון ושני כו', ומקבל טומאה מדרבנן — נקט ליה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:7:1.english: "If with regard to ritual impurity, we require an egg-bulk of food" - [This] implies that food does not contract ritual impurity with less than an egg-bulk. And [regarding] that which Rashi cited from Torat Kohanim [that] food contracts impurity in any amount — as it is taught: "'From any food' [teaches] that it becomes impure in any amount; could it be that it [also] conveys impurity to others [in any amount]? The verse states: 'which may be eaten' — [meaning] food that can be eaten at one time; you must say this is a hen's egg[-bulk]" — Rabbeinu Tam says that it is [merely] an asmakhta [scriptural support], for similarly we include the tithe of vegetables in Torat Kohanim from "and all the tithe of the land," and it is nothing more than a mere asmakhta. And as for that which [the Gemara] challenges in the chapter Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 33b) against the one who says that liquids are absorbed [within the fruit], from what we learned in a Mishnah: "One who is impure through a corpse who pressed olives and grapes [of] an exact egg-bulk, they are pure" — and [the Gemara asks:] if they are absorbed, why are they pure? — and [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring] to grapes that had not yet been rendered susceptible [to impurity]; when do they become susceptible? When he presses them, and when he presses them, their measure is reduced [below an egg-bulk] — [this] works out well even according to the explanation of Rashi, for even though [food] contracts impurity in any amount, nevertheless its measure is reduced from receiving susceptibility [to impurity], according to the explanation of Rabbi Porat, who explains in the name of Rashi in the chapter Chavit (below, Shabbat 145a) that food does not receive susceptibility [to impurity] with less than an egg-bulk, and the reason is because from "which may be eaten" we derive [the requirement of] an egg-bulk to convey impurity to others, and regarding that [same egg-bulk] it is written, "upon which water comes." And similarly in the chapter Eilu Ovrin (Pesachim 45a) regarding dough in the cracks of a kneading trough, where Abaye explains [it as a case] where there is less than an egg-bulk of food and it touched this dough on Passover, where its prohibition makes it significant [so] it joins together [to form an egg-bulk] — even though without joining together [with] less than an egg-bulk, [Abaye] could have established [the case as one] where a creeping creature [sheretz] touched an olive-bulk [of dough] in the cracks of a kneading trough on Passover, where its prohibition makes it significant [so] it contracts impurity — [whereas] on the rest of the days of the year, if he cares about it, yes, [and] if not, no — rather, [the reason he did not establish it that way is] because with regard to contracting impurity itself, nothing practical emerges from it for us, since in any case it is forbidden because of chametz; therefore he chose [to frame it] with regard to conveying impurity to others. And Rabbeinu Tam brings a proof that food does not contract impurity [with] less than an egg-bulk, as it is taught in the chapter Eilu Ovrin (Pesachim 44a): "[If] the porridge is of terumah, [and] the garlic and the oil are of chullin, and a tevul yom [one who immersed that day and awaits sunset] touched part of them, he has disqualified all of them; [if] the porridge is of chullin, and the garlic and oil are of terumah, and a tevul yom touched part of them, he has disqualified only the place of his contact," and we asked about it: Why did he disqualify the place of his contact, seeing that it is not an egg-bulk? And Rashi does not read it thus; rather, he reads: "Seeing that it is nullified in the majority," and he explains that this is what [the Gemara] is asking: Why is the place of his contact disqualified, seeing that the garlic and oil are nullified in the porridge, for because of this [very principle] it teaches in the first clause, "he has disqualified all of them"? And it does not seem right to erase [the text of] the books. Furthermore, granted that they are nullified in the first clause [to be] stringent, [to be] lenient we do not say that they are nullified! And furthermore, it is not applicable to say that the garlic and oil are nullified, since they are intact, as it teaches "he has disqualified only the place of his contact." And furthermore, (as it is taught in the Tosefta): "In what case does this apply? When it is a thick mass in the bowl" — which implies that they are intact. And there is no need to elaborate. And Rashi retracted his view in Keritot (21a), and regarding "a cow contracts food impurity" (Chullin 82a). And as for that which it says in the first chapter of Chullin (24b): "The Torah testified regarding an earthenware vessel, even if it is full of mustard" — "mustard" is not meant literally; rather, it means to say "full of eggs"; and because in mustard there are many [degrees of impurity] — first-degree and second-degree, etc., and it contracts impurity by rabbinic decree — he mentioned it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:7:2.hebrew: אי לענין שבת כגרוגרת בעינן - הוה מצי למיפרך: אמאי נקט זרק, ואמאי נקט תרומה ולבית טמא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:7:2.english: "If [it was raised] with regard to Shabbat, we require a dried fig-bulk" - [The Gemara] could have asked: Why did he specify "threw," and why did he specify "teruma" and "into an impure house"?

Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:7:3.hebrew: כגון דאיכא פחות מכביצה אוכלים כו' - אור"י דלהכי נקט זרק, דהשתא בהדי הדדי קא אתיין, דלא מחייב לענין שבת עד דנח, כדאמר בפרק המוציא (לעיל שבת דף פ.): תוך ג' לרבנן בעיא הנחה על גבי משהו. אבל מכניס — מכי אתי תוך ג', איכא איסור שבת, ואיסור טומאה ליכא עד דמצטרף, ולא אתון בהדי הדדי. ודוקא נקט כזית תרומה, דאיכא איסור לאוכלו בטומאה, אבל פחות מכזית לא; וכן כזית חולין, כיון דאין איסור לאוכלו בטומאה, לא שייך לומר מיגו דמצטרף לענין טומאה — מצטרף לענין שבת. וא"ת: מ"ש כזית תרומה מחצי זית? דהא בתרומה טמאה ליכא אלא עשה, כדמוכח בהערל (יבמות דף ג:), דהאוכלה בטומאת עצמה אינו לוקה, וחצי זית נמי, הא קי"ל כר' יוחנן דחצי שיעור אסור מן התורה (יומא עד.)! וי"ל: דמ"מ כזית חמיר טפי, שהרי זית הוא שיעור ללקות עליו בכל מקום. ודוקא לבית טמא, אבל לבית טהור לא; אע"ג דחשיב ללקות עליו זר האוכלו, מש"ה לא חשיב בפחות מגרוגרת, כיון דאיסור זרות לא בא ע"י הוצאה זו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:7:3.english: "Where there is less than an egg-bulk of food, etc." - Ri says that for this reason [the Gemara] stated "threw" [rather than "brought in"], because now [both prohibitions] come simultaneously, since one is not liable with regard to Shabbat until it comes to rest, as it says in the chapter HaMotzi (above, Shabbat 80a): within three [handbreadths], according to the Rabbis, it requires resting on something. However, [if one] brings [it] in, as soon as it comes within three [handbreadths], there is a Shabbat prohibition, whereas the impurity prohibition is not [yet] present until it joins together [with the food], so they do not come simultaneously. And specifically [the Gemara] stated an olive-bulk of teruma, because there is a prohibition against eating it in [a state of] impurity, whereas [for] less than an olive-bulk there is not; and similarly [for] an olive-bulk of non-sacred food, since there is no prohibition against eating it in [a state of] impurity, it is not applicable to say: "Since it joins together with regard to impurity, it joins together with regard to Shabbat." And if you ask: What is the difference between an olive-bulk of teruma and a half-olive-bulk? For in [the case of] impure teruma there is only a positive commandment, as is proven in [the chapter] HaArel (Yevamot 3b), for one who eats it in its own state of impurity does not incur lashes; and [with regard to] a half-olive-bulk as well, we hold in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan that a half-measure is prohibited by Torah law (Yoma 74a)! One can answer: that nevertheless an olive-bulk is more stringent, since an olive-bulk is the [standard] measure for incurring lashes over it everywhere. And specifically [when thrown] into an impure house, but into a pure house, no; even though it is considered significant [enough] for a non-priest who eats it to incur lashes for it, even so it is not considered significant [enough for Shabbat liability] with less than a dried fig-bulk, since the prohibition of non-priesthood does not come about through this carrying out.

Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:7:4.hebrew: פחות מכביצה אוכלין - ה"ה דה"מ למימר דאיכא כביצה אוכלין, שאין הם צריכין לצירוף וכזית לבד צריך לצירופן. א"נ אור"י, דנקט דוקא פחות מכביצה, אבל כביצה — אפשר דאין מצטרף, כיון שקודם צירוף כבר מטמא, דילמא שבע לה טומאה; דבעיא היא בהקומץ רבה (מנחות כד.) גבי עשרון שחלקו ונטמא אחד מהן והניחו בכלי ונגע טבול יום בטמא, מהו: מי אמר שבע לה טומאה ולא נטמא הטהור — אע"ג דאם היו שניהם טהורים ונגע טבול יום באחד מהן שניהם טמאין, דכלי מצרף מה שבתוכו לקדש — השתא דשבע לה טומאה לא מצטריף, או דילמא לא אמרי' שבע לה טומאה? ומשום דהתם מספקא לן, נקט פחות מכביצה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 91a:7:4.english: Less than an egg-bulk of food - The same applies that [the Gemara] could have said that there is an egg-bulk of food [in the house], for they do not need joining, and only the olive-bulk needs to join with them. Alternatively, Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that [the Gemara] specifically chose "less than an egg-bulk," because [with] an egg-bulk, it is possible that it does not join, since prior to joining it already becomes impure, [for] perhaps "the impurity is sated." For this is an unresolved question in [the chapter] HaKometz Rabbah (Menachot 24a) regarding a tenth [of an ephah] that one divided, and one of them became impure, and he placed them in a vessel, and a tevul yom touched the impure one: what is [the halakha]? Do we say "the impurity is sated" and the pure one does not become impure — even though if both of them were pure and a tevul yom touched one of them, both of them would be impure, since a vessel joins together whatever is inside it for kodesh — now that the impurity is sated, it does not join together; or perhaps we do not say "the impurity is sated"? And because there it is uncertain to us, [the Gemara] chose "less than an egg-bulk."
